messages:
Oncall Bot: [ALERT] service: inference-serving - error-rate spike (>5% 5m) - paging oncall
Oncall Bot: Incident ID: INC-5237 | Runbooks: https://redwood-internal.docs/runbooks/INC-5237
Marie Chen: saw this, paging in. i’m pulling logs now. any visible customer impact?
Samir Patel: yes, tracing shows 502s from model-proxy to runtime, started ~2134567800. Affected requests are mostly long-context hits. trying a quick scale.
Samir Patel: running:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-serving --replicas=12
```
Samir Patel: will also flip fallback to quantized-variant for canary traffic: `route-policy set fallback=quant-q4_0`
Marie Chen: can we squelch alert noise? thresholds are very chatty during bursts. current rule is error_rate>5% over 5m
Nora Kim: suggested: raise to 7% for 5m and add a 30s suppression on flapping, plus increase rolling window to 10m for bucketed aggregates
Triage-Lead: note for post-incident: evaluate metric cardinality — a lot of these are per-model shards. maybe aggregate by model_family
DevOps-Bot: Autoscaler triggered, added 4 pods at 2134567842. CPU stable now.
Samir Patel: after scale, error rate dropped to 2.3% at 2134567875. still seeing a small tail of 502s from nodepool-a
Marie Chen: i'm going to start customer impact checklists: CS/PD notified? any 3rd party alerts?
Eli Vargas: CS pinged at 2134567860, they reported a handful of failed API calls from one large customer (acme-inc). I've opened a case and flagged for retro.
Marie Chen: ok i'll prepare the incident timeline and start the RCA doc. adding links to dashboards and logs.
Marie Chen: dashboards:
- overview: https://console.redwood.ai/d/alerts/overview?panelId=5
- per-shard errors: https://console.redwood.ai/d/alerts/shard-errors?orgId=1
- kv-cache heatmap: https://console.redwood.ai/d/infra/kv-heatmap
Samir Patel: digging into runtime logs — looks like a KV eviction cascade on nodepool-a leading to increased tail latencies and upstream timeouts. opening an issue: EV-248.
Nora Kim: propose alert change: split the error_rate rule into two: one for user-facing 5xxs (threshold 3% 5m) and one for internal proxy timeouts (threshold 7% 10m). that reduces pages for internal transients
Triage-Lead: good call. also add runbook stub for EV-248 with mitigation steps + contact list
Marie Chen: handing over to Eli for next shift. checklist updated and playbook notes added.
Marie Chen: Handoff notes:
- mitigation done: scaled to 12 replicas, routed canary to quantized model, cache warmup scripts kicked
- outstanding: need KV eviction root cause and long-term autoscale tuning
- owners: Samir (EV-248), Nora (alert changes), Eli (customer follow-ups)
Eli Vargas: accepting handoff — I'll own tomorrow's follow-up calls and coordinate with infra.
Eli Vargas: creating a post-incident task list in the runbook and tagging owners.
DevOps-Bot: created ticket EV-248 and linked to INC-5237 at 2134567902
Marie Chen: PR for runbook changes: https://git.redwood.ai/r/runbooks/merge/1123
Marie Chen: runbook updates (summary):
- add `kv-eviction` section with step-by-step `cache-warmup` commands and circuit breaker toggles
- add new alert rules and thresholds: split 5xx vs proxy-timeout
- annotate autoscale thresholds and steady-state targets per model_family
- set oncall ownership for the alert to eng-runtime (primary) and eng-infra (secondary)
Samir Patel: i added a temporary alert suppression rule for nodepool-a to avoid repeats during warmup (expires 24h)
Nora Kim: i'll add dashboard panels for aggregated model_family metrics and a runbook pointer for "how to rehydrate KV caches"
Eli Vargas: will do a short post-call tomorrow 10:00 PST with CS + infra to confirm customer impact closure
Marie Chen: thanks all. marking this thread as resolved for now, will reopen if we see regression. :white_check_mark:
Oncall Bot: Incident INC-5237 marked RESOLVED at 2134567925
